title: First Responder Operator Toolkit: Rate Limit Surges & KV Cache Evictions
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This operator toolkit is a prescriptive runbook for first responders who handle two high-frequency, high-impact incident classes: (A) sudden API rate-limit surges that push latency past SLOs, and (B) kv-cache eviction storms that cause increased cold-start costs, throughput collapse, or model-quality regressions. The goal is to enable fast stabilization, clear customer-facing status messages, and evidence collection for post-incident analysis.

Scope
-----
- Services covered: router, ingest-api, serving-runtime, batcher, kv-cache (redis/managed-kv), autoscaler, routing-proxy
- Excludes: infra-level cloud-provider outages, control-plane-only billing issues (see infra runbooks)
- Audience: on-call first responders (SREs, platform engineers), bridge operators, customer-success for external comms

Pager thresholds (when to page)
--------------------------------
- Pager (P0): sustained 5m 95th latency > 500ms for hosted API endpoints OR error-rate > 2% across edged routes
- Pager (P1): sudden 1m spike in API token rate causing active connections to exceed 85% of provisioned per-customer throughput limits
- Pager (P2): kv-cache eviction rate > 1000 evictions/s sustained for 3m OR cache hit-rate drop > 20 percentage points

Ownership and roles
--------------------
- Primary responder: on-call service owner for serving-runtime or routing team (see team-roster)
- Secondary/Bridge: SRE on-call for the region
- Escalation: Platform lead if not resolved within 30 minutes or cross-region fallback needed
- Customer communications owner: customer-success (tiered) with technical lead for status phrasing

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
----------------------------------------
1. Acknowledge pager and open the incident page (start a temporary incident doc).
2. Set short-term status to "Investigating" on the internal incident board.
3. Capture initial evidence (timestamps, affected services, error types). Run these commands: 

   ```bash
   # request distribution
   curl -sS https://monitoring/api/v1/query?query=api_request_duration_seconds
   # active connections to serving runtime
   kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o wide
   # redis info (if managed, use cloud console)
   redis-cli INFO stats | egrep "evicted_keys|keyspace_hits|keyspace_misses"
   ```

4. Check recent deploys (last 60m): ci-cd dashboard / Git commit list for routes/serving-runtime.
5. Determine if surge is traffic-driven (spike pattern in ingress) or internal (misbehaving consumer/bug).

Runbook: Immediate mitigation (Rate-limit surge)
------------------------------------------------
1. Confirm cause: is the surge from a single tenant (noisy-tenant) or broad traffic spike? Use request tags: tenant_id, api_key_id.
2. If noisy-tenant: apply tenant-level throttling to 10rps or a temporary 429 target via router config. Commands: 

   ```bash
   # apply rate-limit policy (example CLI)
   rrouterctl apply-policy --tenant $TENANT --policy "fixed-window:10rps" --reason "noisy-tenant surge"
   ```

3. If multi-tenant broad spike: enable spillover routing to lower-cost burst pool or autoscaler:

   - Set routing-proxy feature flag: enable_spillover=true
   - If Dedicated pools are saturated, route to hosted fallback model variant (lower-q quantized variant) via routing policy.

4. Reduce non-essential background workload: pause model-evaluation jobs and batcher ingestion for 15m.
5. Increase logging sample rate for 10 minutes to capture request traces for impacted routes.

Runbook: Immediate mitigation (KV cache eviction storm)
-------------------------------------------------------
1. Identify eviction driver:
   - Check cache memory usage, eviction metrics, and keys being evicted (hot keys vs many ephemeral keys).
   - Commands: redis-cli INFO memory; redis-cli CLIENT LIST; monitoring queries for keyspace growth.
2. If caused by key explosion (eg: bad prefixing): apply a short TTL rewrite or prefix filter on writers:

   ```yaml
   # example config snippet for writer service to normalize keys
   key_transform:
     max_prefix_len: 64
     sanitize: true
   ```

3. If due to legitimate increased working set: scale the managed-kv horizontally (increase node count) or switch to provisioned-memory tier. Follow cloud-provider scaling SOP: 

   - Trigger managed-kv scale via cloud console or cli (documented in infra runbook).
   - If autoscaling not fast enough, enable a temporary bypass that sends cold reads to a read-through path in the serving-runtime (adds latency but keeps correctness).

4. If eviction causes model-quality regressions (higher hallucinations or token dropouts), immediately route traffic to a variant with a warm-cold cache sync (sticky routing to warmed nodes) and notify applied-ml team.

Evidence collection (must-haves)
-------------------------------
- Timestamped monitoring screenshots/links (ingress, latency, error rate, eviction rate).
- Representative request traces (one successful, one failed) with request ids.
- Pod/container logs from affected timeline.
- Any recent deploy artifact ids.
- Tenant ids (if noisy tenant) and a sample of offending request patterns.

Customer status templates (use and adapt)
-----------------------------------------
- Immediate short notice (30–60 minutes):

  "We are currently investigating increased latency and intermittent failures affecting text-generation requests in {region}. Our engineers are stabilizing routing and throttling noisy traffic to restore service. We will provide an update within 60 minutes. Affected customers: {list if public}."

- Follow-up extended notice (when mitigation applied):

  "Mitigation applied: rate limiting for identified noisy traffic and spillover routing enabled. Most customers are seeing reduced errors and improved latency. We continue to monitor and will publish a root cause analysis within 72 hours."

- Severity-critical public outage message (if SLO credit likely):

  "Incident summary: sustained service degradation for text-generation endpoints in {region} between {start} and {end}. We are issuing an SLA review and will contact affected customers with next steps and credit calculations."

Status page fields to populate (recommended)
-------------------------------------------
- Incident title, start time, impacted services, customer impact (tiered), status (Investigating/Identified/Mitigated/Resolved), mitigation summary, next update ETA.

Post-incident immediate tasks (first 24h)
----------------------------------------
1. Keep incident page open and transition to "Postmortem in progress".
2. Assign customers affected and hand off to customer-success for outreach within 24h.
3. Preserve forensic evidence (logs, traces) in the incident bucket (immutable) for 30d.
4. Create a short timeline of actions with exact timestamps (automatic via incident logger).

Postmortem template (must include these sections)
------------------------------------------------
- Title and summary (one paragraph).
- Impact: customer-facing effects, telemetry, affected tenants.
- Timeline: accurate to the minute for first 2 hours, then to 5 minutes for remainder.
- Root cause: single paragraph and supporting evidence.
- Contributing factors: configs, human, tooling, ops.
- Mitigations applied (short-term / medium-term / long-term).
- Action items (owner, due date, verification criteria).
- Compensation (if applicable) and PR contact.

Postmortem verification checklist
--------------------------------
- [ ] Incident page closed and linked to postmortem
- [ ] Evidence preserved and tagged
- [ ] Action owners assigned and calendar invites scheduled
- [ ] Customer outreach templates approved and sent
- [ ] Runbook updated (if changes identified)

Game day scenario (playbook exercise)
------------------------------------
- Objective: practice noisy-tenant detection and application of tenant-level throttling, plus eviction mitigation flow.
- Participants: serving-runtime oncall (primary), SRE bridge (secondary), customer-success, applied-ml observer.
- Setup: run a synthetic noisy client that ramps a single tenant to 10x normal RPS and simultaneously creates key explosion for the cache namespace.
- Success criteria: incident detected and acknowledged within 5 minutes, throttle applied within 10 minutes, eviction rate reduced to baseline within 20 minutes, customer-status posted within 30 minutes.
- Debrief: review evidence, confirm runbook accuracy, update playbook with observed gaps.

Runbook snippets and safe commands (cheat sheet)
------------------------------------------------
- Check current request distribution (promql):
  api_request_rate{region="us-west-2"} by (tenant_id, api_key_id)

- Apply tenant throttle (router CLI):
  rrouterctl apply-policy --tenant {TENANT} --policy "fixed-window:10rps" --reason "emergency-throttle"

- Scale managed-kv nodes (example provider CLI):
  mgkvctl scale --cluster-id {CLUSTER} --replicas 3

- Pause background batches (k8s job):
  kubectl -n prod scale job batcher --replicas=0

- Route to fallback quantized model variant (feature-flag approach):
  curl -X POST https://routing/api/v1/route --data '{"route":"fallback-quantized","match":"*"}'

Guidelines for customer-success communications
--------------------------------------------
- Keep updates factual, avoid technical blame in public messages.
- Use tiered messaging: private customers get more detailed timelines and dedicated contact.
- Offer remediation/credit language only after coordination with finance and legal.
- Template library: keep 3 templates (initial, mitigation, resolution) and a customizable technical annex for flagged customers.

Runbook governance and review cadence
-----------------------------------
- This playbook must be exercised during at least one quarterly game day and reviewed after any production incident.
- Changes to mitigation defaults (e.g., default tenant throttle rates) require approval from platform lead and an annotated rollout plan for 48h canary.

Appendix: sample evidence collection checklist (one-line items)
-------------------------------------------------------------
- Incident ID:
- Pager signal and raw metric link:
- Top 10 tenants by request rate during incident window:
- Redis INFO snapshot at T0 and T+5m:
- Pod restart/crash loop evidence:
- Deployed artifacts and commit SHAs in last 2 hours:
- Customer-impact mapping and contact owner:
